mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship holds as long as monetary policy is the primary driver of equity returns.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day forward returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and returns is not significantly negative (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 5.0%, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%, or the average 5-day return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals a deepening economic slowdown where monetary easing fails to offset supply-side contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for the interaction term (FEDFUNDS and INDPRO both declining) falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the 60-day return in interaction-triggered periods is not significantly negative (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 4.5%), the S&P 500 experiences negative 20-day forward returns due to reduced liquidity and higher discount rates for equities.
failure_condition: The average 20-day return during FEDFUNDS > 4.5% periods is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05), or the return in these periods is not more negative than in non-tightening periods (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) indicates weakening demand for residential construction, reducing economic activity and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for HOUST as a predictor of 5-day forward returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between HOUST and returns is not significantly negative (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) falls below 370,000 million dollars, it signals a significant drop in consumer spending that reduces corporate revenue growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS < 370000, or the average 60-day return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a supply contraction regime (INDPRO falling below 100), the S&P 500 experiences negative 20-day forward returns due to reduced economic output and corporate production capacity.
failure_condition: The average 20-day return during INDPRO < 100 periods is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05), or the return in these periods is not more negative than in non-contraction periods (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates weakening labor market conditions that reduce consumer income and spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for PAYEMS as a predictor of 5-day forward returns falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between PAYEMS and returns is not significantly negative (p>0.05).
